hypotheses.title: semtypes env.typeAtom never deduplicates atoms (atomTable keyed by fresh pointer), so structurally identical types get distinct cell/list/mapping atoms and defeat BDD identity shortcuts and memos
hypotheses.issue: semtypes/env.go:(*env).typeAtom is documented as interning atoms by value, but atomTable is map[AtomicType]typeAtom and every AtomicType implementation is a pointer (*cellAtomicType, *ListAtomicType, *MappingAtomicType, *functionAtomicType). Every caller passes &local of a freshly built struct, so the lookup essentially never hits: on the reproducer, 240,881 typeAtom calls had 6 hits, and 150k cell atoms were created for at most 165 structurally distinct cells. Each miss takes the global atomTableMutex and grows a map that keeps every atom alive. Worse, every occurrence of a type descriptor such as Item[], [Item,int] or map<Item> (resolveBTypeInner) gets fresh atoms, so structurally identical types have different BDDs. internBddNodeKey then interns more keys, the identity and same-atom shortcuts in bdd_common_ops never fire, and the per-Context list/mapping memos miss. Every assignment or argument subtype check (stage 5, and stage 6 validateResolvedType -> IsSubtype, about 12% of CPU on the reproducer) does a full BDD emptiness check.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate repro.bal: N local declarations whose explicit type descriptors are
structurally identical (Item[], [Item, int], map<Item>). Every occurrence makes
semtypes mint brand-new cell/list/mapping atoms (env.typeAtom never dedupes),
and every `T xI = x(I-1)` then needs a full BDD subtype check in stage 6."""
import sys
N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 30000
out = []
out.append("type Item record {| int id; string name; decimal price = 0; string[] tags = []; |};\n")
out.append("function use(any v) { _ = v; }\n")
out.append("public function main() {")
out.append("    Item[] a0 = [];")
out.append("    [Item, int] b0 = [{id: 0, name: \"\"}, 0];")
out.append("    map<Item> c0 = {};")
for i in range(1, N):
    out.append(f"    Item[] a{i} = a{i-1};")
    out.append(f"    [Item, int] b{i} = b{i-1};")
    out.append(f"    map<Item> c{i} = c{i-1};")
out.append(f"    use(a{N-1}); use(b{N-1}); use(c{N-1});")
out.append("}")
print("\n".join(out))
reproducer.command: python3 gen_repro.py 30000 > repro.bal; go build -o bal ./cli/cmd; hyperfine -w1 -r5 -N './bal run repro.bal'; ./bin/benchmark --mode time|memory --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> repro.bal

hypotheses.fix_approach: Prototype: add a structural key for cell atoms: mutability, the member SemType's all/some bits, and the canonical BDD key of each subtype, uvarint-encoded into a string. If any subtype is not a BDD, the key is empty and the old behaviour applies. Keep a second map, cellAtomShapes, in env. A new sharedCellAtom, used only by cellContainingWithEnvSemTypeCellMutability, first looks up atomTable by pointer, then cellAtomShapes by shape, and otherwise creates the atom (index still len(atomTable)) and records it in both maps. After freeze, the shape map is read lock-free like atomTable. Ephemeral atoms are never recorded, and their canonical keys carry a generation number of at least 1, so they cannot collide with frozen shapes. Pitfalls: (1) sharing list/mapping atoms is NOT behaviour-preserving today. semantics/internal/types/type_resolver.go keys record defaults and method tables by mapping atom (mappingDefaultsByHandle, methodTablesByHandle), so records with identical fields but different defaults collide (wrong output, nil deref). The 'ambiguous inherent type for list/mapping constructor' diagnostics also rely on atom identity, and BIR union member order changes with atom indices. Those dependencies must be removed first to get the larger win (about -29%). (2) The env init code and env_init_test expect pointer-identity atoms for predefined types, so keep cellAtom/listAtom pointer-keyed for env setup. (3) A real fix could avoid string keys by using a comparable struct key or by hash-consing member SemTypes.
